# CIFAR-10 kept as uint8 tensors on the GPU; we divide by 255 per batch -> pixels in [0, 1]
def load_cifar():
    tr = CIFAR10("data", train=True, download=True)
    te = CIFAR10("data", train=False, download=True)
    to_t = lambda ds: torch.from_numpy(ds.data).permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
    return to_t(tr), to_t(te)

train_u8, test_u8 = load_cifar()
if QUICK:
    train_u8, test_u8 = train_u8[:2000], test_u8[:500]
train_u8, test_u8 = train_u8.to(device), test_u8.to(device)
print(train_u8.shape, test_u8.shape)

def to01(x_u8):
    return x_u8.float() / 255.0

def batches(data, bs, shuffle=True):
    if shuffle:
        idx = torch.randperm(len(data), device=data.device)
        for i in range(0, len(data) - bs + 1, bs):
            yield to01(data[idx[i:i + bs]])
    else:
        for i in range(0, len(data), bs):
            yield to01(data[i:i + bs])

def psnr(a, b):
    # a, b in [0,1]; PSNR per image, then averaged
    mse = ((a - b) ** 2).flatten(1).mean(1).clamp_min(1e-10)
    return (10 * torch.log10(1.0 / mse)).mean().item()

# FID: standard 2048-d InceptionV3 features, real statistics = the 10k CIFAR-10 test images
from torchmetrics.image.fid import FrechetInceptionDistance

class FIDScorer:
    def __init__(self, real_u8):
        self.fid_device = "cpu" if device == "mps" else device
        self.m = FrechetInceptionDistance(feature=2048, reset_real_features=False, normalize=True).to(self.fid_device)
        for i in range(0, len(real_u8), 500):
            self.m.update(to01(real_u8[i:i + 500]).to(self.fid_device), real=True)

    def __call__(self, fake):
        # fake: float tensor in [0,1], shape (N,3,32,32)
        self.m.reset()                       # real stats are kept
        for i in range(0, len(fake), 500):
            self.m.update(fake[i:i + 500].to(self.fid_device).clamp(0, 1), real=False)
        return float(self.m.compute())

fid_score = FIDScorer(test_u8)
N_FID = 500 if QUICK else 10000     # number of generated images used for FID

def show(imgs, nrow=8, title=None, size=7):
    g = make_grid(imgs[:nrow * nrow].cpu(), nrow=nrow, padding=1)
    plt.figure(figsize=(size, size)); plt.imshow(g.permute(1, 2, 0).numpy()); plt.axis("off")
    if title: plt.title(title)
    plt.show()

Part B¶

Assignment 2 - Part B: WGAN and WGAN-GP on CIFAR-10¶

Data is read as [0, 1] like the rest of the assignment; right before it goes into the critic we map it to [-1, 1] so it matches the generator's tanh output (real and fake have to live in the same range, otherwise the critic can just tell them apart by scale). Generated images are mapped back to [0, 1] for FID and plots.

  • WGAN: weight clipping (c = 0.01), RMSprop lr 5e-5, 5 critic steps per generator step, critic has no normalization layers.
  • WGAN-GP: gradient penalty λ = 10, Adam (lr 1e-4, β = (0, 0.9)), 5 critic steps per generator step, critic uses LayerNorm-style GroupNorm(1) (no BatchNorm in the critic with GP).

Same generator in both runs. FID (2048-d Inception features, test set as reference) is tracked during training with 5k samples and computed at the end with 10k samples.

In [15]:
ZDIM = 128

class Generator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, zdim=ZDIM, base=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.base = base
        self.fc = nn.Linear(zdim, base * 8 * 4 * 4)
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.BatchNorm2d(base * 8), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(base * 8, base * 4, 4, 2, 1), nn.BatchNorm2d(base * 4), nn.ReLU(),   # 8
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(base * 4, base * 2, 4, 2, 1), nn.BatchNorm2d(base * 2), nn.ReLU(),   # 16
            nn.ConvTranspose2d(base * 2, 3, 4, 2, 1), nn.Tanh())                                     # 32

    def forward(self, z):
        return self.net(self.fc(z).view(-1, self.base * 8, 4, 4))


class Critic(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, base=64, norm=False):
        super().__init__()
        N = (lambda c: nn.GroupNorm(1, c)) if norm else (lambda c: nn.Identity())
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(3, base * 2, 4, 2, 1), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),                                      # 16
            nn.Conv2d(base * 2, base * 4, 4, 2, 1), N(base * 4), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),                  # 8
            nn.Conv2d(base * 4, base * 8, 4, 2, 1), N(base * 8), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2),                  # 4
            nn.Flatten(), nn.Linear(base * 8 * 16, 1))

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x).view(-1)


def init_weights(m):
    if isinstance(m, (nn.Conv2d, nn.ConvTranspose2d, nn.Linear)):
        nn.init.normal_(m.weight, 0.0, 0.02)
        if m.bias is not None: nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)


def grad_penalty(D, real, fake):
    a = torch.rand(real.size(0), 1, 1, 1, device=device)
    mix = (a * real + (1 - a) * fake).requires_grad_(True)
    g, = torch.autograd.grad(D(mix).sum(), mix, create_graph=True)
    return ((g.flatten(1).norm(2, dim=1) - 1) ** 2).mean()


@torch.no_grad()
def gen_images(G, n, bs=500):
    G.eval()
    out = [((G(torch.randn(min(bs, n - i), ZDIM, device=device)) + 1) / 2).clamp(0, 1).cpu() for i in range(0, n, bs)]
    G.train()
    return torch.cat(out)
In [16]:
ITERS = 200 if QUICK else 40000        # generator updates
EVAL_EVERY = 100 if QUICK else 4000
BS, N_CRITIC = 64, 5
N_FID_TRACK = 500 if QUICK else 5000
fixed_z = torch.randn(64, ZDIM, device=device)


def train_gan(mode):
    seed_all()
    G = Generator().to(device); G.apply(init_weights)
    D = Critic(norm=(mode == "wgan-gp")).to(device); D.apply(init_weights)
    if mode == "wgan":
        oG = torch.optim.RMSprop(G.parameters(), lr=5e-5)
        oD = torch.optim.RMSprop(D.parameters(), lr=5e-5)
    else:
        oG = torch.optim.Adam(G.parameters(), lr=1e-4, betas=(0.0, 0.9))
        oD = torch.optim.Adam(D.parameters(), lr=1e-4, betas=(0.0, 0.9))

    log = dict(it=[], w_dist=[], fid_it=[], fid=[])
    t_start = time.time()
    for it in range(1, ITERS + 1):
        for _ in range(N_CRITIC):
            real = to01(train_u8[torch.randint(len(train_u8), (BS,), device=device)]) * 2 - 1
            with torch.no_grad():
                fake = G(torch.randn(BS, ZDIM, device=device))
            d_real, d_fake = D(real).mean(), D(fake).mean()
            loss_d = d_fake - d_real
            if mode == "wgan-gp":
                loss_d = loss_d + 10.0 * grad_penalty(D, real, fake)
            oD.zero_grad(set_to_none=True); loss_d.backward(); oD.step()
            if mode == "wgan":
                for p in D.parameters():
                    p.data.clamp_(-0.01, 0.01)

        loss_g = -D(G(torch.randn(BS, ZDIM, device=device))).mean()
        oG.zero_grad(set_to_none=True); loss_g.backward(); oG.step()

        if it % 100 == 0:
            log["it"].append(it); log["w_dist"].append((d_real - d_fake).item())
        if it % EVAL_EVERY == 0 or it == ITERS:
            f = fid_score(gen_images(G, N_FID_TRACK))
            log["fid_it"].append(it); log["fid"].append(f)
            print(f"[{mode}] iter {it:6d}  W-dist est {(d_real - d_fake).item():7.3f}  FID({N_FID_TRACK}) {f:6.1f}  "
                  f"elapsed {(time.time() - t_start) / 60:.1f} min")
    log["train_sec"] = time.time() - t_start
    return G, log
In [18]:
results, gens = {}, {}
for mode in ["wgan", "wgan-gp"]:
    print("=" * 20, mode, "=" * 20)
    G, log = train_gan(mode)
    t0 = time.time(); imgs = gen_images(G, N_FID); log["sample_sec"] = time.time() - t0
    log["final_fid"] = fid_score(imgs)
    log["sec_per_1k_iters"] = log["train_sec"] / ITERS * 1000
    print(f"--> {mode}: final FID (N={N_FID}) = {log['final_fid']:.2f}\n")
    results[mode], gens[mode] = log, G
    torch.save(G.state_dict(), OUT / "models" / f"{mode}_gen.pt")
    save_image(imgs[:100], OUT / "figs" / f"{mode}_100.png", nrow=10, padding=1)

json.dump(results, open(OUT / "partB_wgan.json", "w"), indent=1)

WGAN observations¶

WGAN-GP reached a final FID of 41.45, compared with 80.49 for weight-clipped WGAN. Its samples show clearer object structure in the displayed grids. WGAN-GP took 134.57 minutes to train; WGAN took 66.57 minutes. A GAN has no encoder in this implementation, so reconstruction PSNR does not apply. These results use the saved full-run outputs above; recalculate them in the required lab run.
